P1para.Text: These Regulations may be cited as the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000 (Market Abuse) Regulations 2016 and shall come into force on 3rd July 2016.
In these Regulations the employer shall ensure that every worker receives adequate information about market abuse provisions and their obligations under these Regulations.

The competent authority shall maintain a register of all persons who have been granted permission to carry out regulated activities. Every operator of a trading venue must notify the competent authority of any suspected instances of market abuse.

A person who manages or operates a trading venue shall establish and maintain effective arrangements, systems and procedures aimed at preventing and detecting insider dealing, market manipulation and attempted insider dealing and market manipulation. The operator shall train all employees in the detection of suspicious transactions and orders.

The worker who discovers or suspects a breach of these Regulations has the right to report it to the competent authority without fear of retaliation. The employer shall protect whistleblowers from any form of discrimination or disadvantage arising from their disclosure.

The Secretary of State may by order amend the schedule to these Regulations to add, remove or modify the descriptions of instruments or behaviours that constitute market abuse. Any person who is professionally arranging or executing transactions shall maintain records of all orders and transactions for a period of not less than five years.

The local authority shall cooperate with the competent authority in the enforcement of these Regulations. The director or officer of a company who knowingly permits market abuse is guilty of an offence. Every manufacturer of financial instruments shall disclose the terms and conditions associated with such instruments. The supplier of market data shall ensure accuracy and timeliness of information provided to the market.

The inspector appointed under these Regulations may require any person to produce documents and provide explanations. The contractor engaged by an operator shall comply with the same obligations as the operator in relation to record-keeping and reporting. Where a sub-contractor is responsible for maintaining trading systems, they shall ensure that those systems comply with the requirements of these Regulations.

The Health and Safety Executive shall have regard to these Regulations when carrying out its functions in relation to financial services workplaces. The owner of premises where regulated activities take place shall ensure that adequate facilities are provided for the maintenance of proper records. Any employee who fails to comply with a requirement imposed under these Regulations is liable on summary conviction to a fine.

The occupier of any premises used for the purposes of carrying on a regulated activity shall ensure that the premises are suitable for that purpose. The importer of financial products from outside the United Kingdom shall comply with the requirements of Part 3 of these Regulations.
